# Laplace Transform

## F.T. Limitation

<div style="color:#994C01;">
Q1. What is the F.T. of $u(t) \cdot e^{-t}$?
</div>

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    >=latex,
    axis/.style={->, thick, black},
    orange/.style={orange!60!black}
]

\begin{scope}[xshift=2cm, yshift=-2cm]
    % axes
    \draw[axis] (-1,0) -- (3,0) node[right] {$t$};
    \draw[axis] (0,-1) -- (0,2) node[above] {$e^{-t}$};

    \draw[domain=-0:2, smooth, variable=\x, blue] plot ({\x}, {e^(-\x)});

    \node[blue, left] at (-0.1, 1) {$1$};
\end{scope}

\begin{scope}[xshift=8cm, yshift=-2cm]
    % axes
    \draw[axis] (-1,0) -- (3,0) node[right] {$t$};
    \draw[axis] (0,-1) -- (0,2) node[above] {$u(t)$};

    \draw[blue, thick] (-1,0) -- (0,0);
    \draw[blue, thick] (0,0) -- (0,1);
    \draw[blue, thick] (0,1) -- (2,1);

    \node[blue, left] at (-0.1, 1) {$1$};
\end{scope}
\end{tikzpicture}
```


\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{F}[u(t) \cdot e^{-t}] &= \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} u(t) \cdot e^{-t} \cdot e^{-i\omega t} \,dt \\
    &= \int_{0}^{+\infty} e^{-(1 + i\omega) t} \,dt \\
    &= \left. -\frac{1}{1 + i\omega} e^{-(1 + i\omega) t} \right\rvert_{0}^{+\infty} \\
    &= 0 + \frac{1}{1 + i\omega} \cdot \color{red} \frac{1-i\omega}{1-i\omega} \\
    &= \frac{1 - i\omega}{1 + \omega^2} \\
    &= \frac{1}{1 + \omega^2} + \frac{-i\omega}{1 + \omega^2} .
\end{align*}

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    >=latex,
    axis/.style={->, thick, black},
    orange/.style={orange!60!black}
]

\begin{scope}[xshift=-4cm, yshift=-2cm]
    % axes
    \draw[axis] (-3,0) -- (3,0) node[right] {$\omega$};
    \draw[axis] (0,-1) -- (0,2) node[above] {Re};

    \draw[domain=-3:3, smooth, variable=\x, orange] plot ({\x}, {1/(1 + (\x)^2)});

    \node[orange, left] at (-0.1, 1.2) {$1$};
\end{scope}

\begin{scope}[xshift=4cm, yshift=-2cm]
    % axes
    \draw[axis] (-3,0) -- (3,0) node[right] {$\omega$};
    \draw[axis] (0,-1) -- (0,2) node[above] {Im};

    \draw[domain=-3:3, smooth, variable=\x, orange] plot ({\x}, {-\x/(1 + (\x)^2)});
\end{scope}
\end{tikzpicture}
```

<div style="color:#994C01;">
 <br>
Q2. What is the F.T. of $u(t)$?
</div>

\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{F}[u(t)] &= \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} u(t) \cdot e^{-i\omega t} \,dt \\
    &= \int_{0}^{+\infty} e^{-i\omega t} \,dt \\
    &= \left. -\frac{1}{i\omega} e^{-i\omega t} \right\rvert_{0}^{+\infty} \\
    &= -\frac{1}{i\omega} \big(\color{red}\underset{\text{value}}{\underset{\text{undetermined}}{\underline{\color{black}e^{-i\omega\infty}}}} \color{black} - 1\big)
\end{align*}

<div style="text-align: center">

```{.tikz}

    >=latex,
    axis/.style={->, thick, black}
]

\begin{scope}[xshift=-1.5cm, yshift=-1.5cm]

    \draw[axis] (0,-1.5) -- (0,1.5) node[above] {Im};

    \draw[domain=0:2*pi,samples=500, red, thick] plot ({deg(\x)}:1);

    \node[red, left] at (-0.1, 1.2) {$1$};
\end{scope}

\node[red] at (-0.5,-0.5) {$e^{-i\omega t}$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

</div>

<div style="color:#994C01;">
Q3. What is the F.T. of $e^t \cdot u(t)$?
</div>

\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{F}[e^t \cdot u(t)] &= \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} e^t \cdot u(t) \cdot e^{-i\omega t} \,dt \\
    &= \int_{0}^{+\infty} e^{(1 - i\omega) t} \,dt \\
    &= \left. \frac{1}{1 - i\omega} e^{(1 - i\omega) t} \right\rvert_{0}^{+\infty} \\
    &= \frac{1}{1 - i\omega} \cdot (\infty - 1)
\end{align*}

<div style="text-align: center">

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    >=latex,
    axis/.style={->, thick, black}
]

\begin{scope}[xshift=-1.5cm, yshift=-1.5cm]

    \draw[axis] (0,-1.5) -- (0,1.5) node[above] {Im};

    \draw[domain=0:4*pi,samples=500, red, thick] plot ({deg(\x)}:\x/10);

    \node[red, left] at (-0.1, 1.2) {$1$};
\end{scope}

\end{tikzpicture}
```

</div>


## Laplace Transform

The premise of F.T. is that $f(t)$ must be convergent.

<div style="color:red;">
<u>What if $f(t)$ is not convergent?</u>
</div>

\begin{align*}
    & \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} u(t) \cdot \color{red}\underbrace{\color{blue} e^{-\sigma t} \color{black} \cdot e^{-i\omega t}} \color{black} \,dt \\
    =& \int_{\color{red}{0}}^{+\infty} u(t) \cdot \color{red}{e^{-(\sigma + i\omega) t}} \color{black} \,dt
\end{align*}

Define $s = \sigma + i\omega$

$$\mathcal{L}[f(t)] = \int_{0}^{+\infty} f(t) \cdot e^{-st} \,dt .$$

\begin{array}{ll}
    \text{L.T.: } & f(t) \div e^{\sigma t} \text{ to find } e^{\sigma t} \text{ in } f(t) \\
    & f(t) \div e^{i\omega t} \text{ to find AC components at } \omega.
\end{array}

\usepackage{cancel}

::: {layout-ncol=2}
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{L}[u(t)] &= \int_{0}^{+\infty} \color{red}\cancel{\color{black}u(t)} \color{black} \cdot e^{-st} \,dt \\
    &= -\frac{1}{s} \cdot e^{-st} \bigg\rvert_{0}^{+\infty} \\
    &= 0 + \frac{1}{s}
\end{align*}

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    >=latex,
    axis/.style={->, thick, black}
]
    % axes
    \draw[axis] (-1.5,0) -- (1.5,0) node[right] {$\sigma$};
    \draw[axis] (0,-1.5) -- (0,1.5) node[above] {$j\omega$};

    \fill[red] (0,0) circle (2pt);
\end{tikzpicture}
```
:::

::: {layout-ncol=2}
<span style="color:green;">
$s=1$: $\displaystyle \int_{0}^{+\infty} e^{-t} \,dt = 1$.
</span><br>
<span style="color:#994C01;">
$s=2$: $\displaystyle \int_{0}^{+\infty} e^{-2t} \,dt = \frac{1}{2}$.
</span><br>
<span style="color:red;">
$s=3$: $\displaystyle \int_{0}^{+\infty} e^{-3t} \,dt = \frac{1}{3}$.
</span><br>
<span style="color:blue;">
$s=0$: $\displaystyle \frac{1}{0} = \infty$.
</span>

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    >=latex,
    axis/.style={->, thick, black}
]
    % axes
    \draw[axis] (-0.5,0) -- (3.5,0) node[right] {$t$};
    \draw[axis] (0,-1.5) -- (0,1.5) node[above] {$u(t) \cdot e^{-st}$};

    \draw[domain=0:3, smooth, variable=\x, blue, thick] plot ({\x}, {1});
    \draw[domain=0:3, smooth, variable=\x, green, thick] plot ({\x}, {e^(-\x)});
    \draw[domain=0:3, smooth, variable=\x, orange!60!black, thick] plot ({\x}, {e^(-2*\x)});
    \draw[domain=0:3, smooth, variable=\x, red, thick] plot ({\x}, {e^(-3*\x)});

    \node[blue, right] at (3, 1.2) {$s=0$};
    \node[blue, right] at (3, 0.8) {$e^{0t}$};
    \node[black, left] at (-0.1, 1) {$1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
:::

::: {layout-ncol=2}
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{L}[e^t] &= \int_{0}^{+\infty} \cancel{u(t)} \cdot e^t \cdot e^{-st} \,dt \\
    &= \int_{0}^{+\infty} e^{(1-s)t} \,dt \\
    &= \left. \frac{1}{1-s} e^{(1-s)t} \right\rvert_{0}^{+\infty} \\
    &= 0 - \frac{1}{1-s} \\
    &= \frac{1}{s-1}
\end{align*}

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    >=latex,
    axis/.style={->, thick, black}
]
    % axes
    \draw[axis] (-1.5,0) -- (1.5,0) node[right] {$\sigma$};
    \draw[axis] (0,-1.5) -- (0,1.5) node[above] {$j\omega$};

    \fill[red] (1,0) circle (2pt);
    \node[red, below] at (1, -0.1) {$1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
:::

<div style="color:blue;">
When $s=1$, $\mathcal{L}[e^t] = \displaystyle\frac{1}{0} = \infty$, meaning that the original function contains $\underline{\underline{e^t}}$.
</div>


## Why do we need to find exponentials?

<ul style="list-style-type: '① ';">
<li>LTI system is differential equations (D.E.)</li>

::: {layout-ncol=2}
```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}[thick, >=latex]

% Coordinates
\coordinate (A) at (0,0);
\coordinate (B) at (0,3);
\coordinate (C) at (4,3);
\coordinate (D) at (4,0);

% Left side: battery
\draw (A) -- (0,1.1);
\draw (-0.35,1.1) -- (0.35,1.1);   % short plate
\draw (-0.55,1.45) -- (0.55,1.45); % long plate
\draw (0,1.45) -- (B);
\node[left] at (-0.5,1.3) {$V_i$};

% Top side: inductor, concave-down loops
\draw (B) -- (1.0,3);

\draw (1.0,3)
  arc[start angle=180, end angle=0, radius=0.3]
  arc[start angle=180, end angle=0, radius=0.3]
  arc[start angle=180, end angle=0, radius=0.3]
  arc[start angle=180, end angle=0, radius=0.3];

\draw (3.4,3) -- (C);
\node[below] at (2.2,2.8) {$L$};
\node[above, red] at (2.2,3.4) {$V_L$};

% Right side: resistor
\draw (C) -- (4,2.4);

\draw (4,2.4) -- (3.7,2.2)
              -- (4.3,1.9)
              -- (3.7,1.6)
              -- (4.3,1.3)
              -- (3.7,1.0)
              -- (4,0.8);

\draw (4,0.8) -- (D);
\node[left] at (3.65,1.6) {$R$};
\node[right,red] at (4.35,1.6) {$V_R$};

% Bottom wire
\draw (D) -- (A);

\node[below, red] at (2,0) {$V_L = L \cdot \frac{di(t)}{dt}$};
\node[below, red] at (2,-1) {$V_R = R \cdot i(t)$};

\end{tikzpicture}
```

<div>
<b>KVL</b>:<br>
$$\underset{\text{D.E.}}{\underbrace{V_i = L \cdot \frac{di(t)}{dt} + R \cdot i(t)}}$$
</div>

:::

::: {layout-ncol=2}
```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}[thick, >=latex]

% Overall reference size similar to previous circuit: about 4 x 3
% Coordinates
\coordinate (O) at (0,0);
\coordinate (WallTop) at (0,3);
\coordinate (MassCenter) at (3.2,0.7);

% Left wall
\draw (0,0) -- (0,2.2);

% Bottom wall / floor
\draw (0,0) -- (4.5,0);

% Wall hatching
\foreach \y in {0.2,0.5,...,2.2} {
    \draw (-0.25,\y-0.15) -- (0,\y+0.1);
}

% Floor hatching
\foreach \x in {0.3,0.6,...,4.3} {
    \draw (\x-0.15,-0.25) -- (\x+0.1,0);
}

% Mass block
\draw (2.6,0.1) rectangle (3.8,1.3);
\node[below] at (3.2,0.7) {$m$};

% Spring from wall to mass
\draw (0,0.7) -- (0.45,0.7);

\draw (0.45,0.7)
    -- (0.60,0.95)
    -- (0.90,0.45)
    -- (1.20,0.95)
    -- (1.50,0.45)
    -- (1.80,0.95)
    -- (2.10,0.45)
    -- (2.40,0.95)
    -- (2.55,0.7);

\draw (2.55,0.7) -- (2.6,0.7);

% Force arrow from center of gravity of mass
\draw[->, blue] (MassCenter) -- (4.5,0.7);
\node[above, blue] at (4.05,0.7) {$F$};

\node[below, red] at (2,-0.5) {spring force: $-kx$};
\node[below, red] at (2,-1) {resistance force: $-\alpha \cdot \dot{x}$};

\end{tikzpicture}
```

<div>
<b>NSL</b>:<br>
$$\underset{\text{D.E.}}{\underbrace{F - kx - \alpha \cdot \dot{x} = m \cdot \ddot{x}}}$$
</div>

:::
</ul>

<ul style="list-style-type: '② ';">
<li>Solutions to D.E. must be either \begin{cases}
    \text{Exponential: } & e^{at} \\
    \text{Sinusoid: } & \sin(\omega t)
\end{cases}</li>

</ul>

\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{L}[\cos(\omega t)] &= \int_{0}^{+\infty} \cos(\omega t) \cdot e^{-st} \,dt \\
    &= \frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{+\infty} \left(e^{i\omega t} + e^{-i\omega t}\right) \cdot e^{-st} \,dt \\
    &= \frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{+\infty} \left[e^{-(s - i\omega) t} + e^{-(s + i\omega) t}\right] \,dt \\
    &= \frac{1}{2} \left.\left[ -\frac{1}{s - i\omega} \cdot e^{-(s - i\omega) t} - \frac{1}{s + i\omega} \cdot e^{-(s + i\omega) t} \right] \right\rvert_{0}^{+\infty} \\
    &= \frac{1}{2} \left[ \frac{1}{s - i\omega} + \frac{1}{s + i\omega} \right] \\
    &= \frac{s}{s^2 + \omega^2}
\end{align*}

::: {layout-ncol=2}

\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{L}[t \cdot u(t)] &= \int_{0}^{+\infty} t \cdot e^{-st} \,dt \\
    &= \int_{0}^{+\infty} -\frac{1}{s} \cdot t \,de^{-st} \\
    &= -\frac{1}{s} \int_{0}^{\infty} t \cdot \,de^{-st} \\
    &= -\frac{1}{s} \left[ t \cdot e^{-st} \bigg\rvert_{0}^{\infty} - \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-st} \,dt \right] \\
    &= -\frac{1}{s} \left[ \cancel{0 - 0} - \left(-\frac{1}{s}\right)\cdot e^{-st} \bigg\rvert_{0}^{\infty} \right] \\
    &= -\frac{1}{s} \cdot \frac{1}{s} \cdot (0-1) \\
    &= \frac{1}{s^2}
\end{align*}

<span style="color:green;">Side notes:</span>
\begin{align*}
    \color{green}(xy)' \,&\color{green}= x'y + xy' \\
    \color{green}xy \,&\color{green}= \int x\,dy + \int y\,dx \\
    \color{green}\int x\,dy \,&\color{green}= xy - \int y\,dx
\end{align*}

:::
